items.title: Privacy-preserving usage-evidence envelope shape + builder
items.context: In a new core/usage-ledger/authority-evidence.ts (pure; imports only ./ siblings + node), define a PrivacyPreservingUsageEvidenceEnvelope type and buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) that encodes a ledger record as digests (e.g. sha256 of the canonical record via canonical-json.ts) + non-secret fields (model, provider name, usage counts, source, correlation ids, decision) needed for a future Authority submission. MUST contain NO raw prompt/transcript/secret/key/auth-header (reuse the privacy denylist / reject if present). Unit-tested: envelope built from a record contains a recordDigest + allowed fields and zero forbidden material.

happy.desc: buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(validRecord) returns envelope with recordDigest (non-empty hex string, matches sha256 of canonicalJson(record)) + allowlisted fields (model, provider.name, usage.source, usage.inputTokens, usage.outputTokens, usage.cacheCreationInputTokens, usage.cacheReadInputTokens, decision.kind, recordId, ledgerCallId, attemptId, sequence) -> all present and matching the source record; WHY: proves the envelope faithfully mirrors non-secret fields and computes a stable digest

buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) deep-scanned for ZERO forbidden material: JSON.stringify(envelope).toLowerCase() does NOT contain any of the FORBIDDEN_FIELD_NAMES tokens (prompt, transcript, secret, apiKey, authorizationHeader, rawResponse, content, messages, password, credentials, bearerToken, accessToken, refreshToken, etc.) AND the envelope object has no key at any depth whose lowercased name is in the denylist -> assertion passes; WHY: the anti-leak gate is the whole point

edge.desc: buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) where record has extra nested metadata containing a forbidden field name (e.g. record.metadata.debug.rawPrompt) -> builder either rejects (throws/returns error) OR the envelope omits the forbidden field entirely; the envelope NEVER contains the forbidden material; WHY: tests that forbidden fields in arbitrary nesting depths are caught, not just top-level

buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) where usage.source is unavailable and all token dimensions are null -> envelope still has a valid recordDigest and source=unavailable with null token fields; WHY: boundary case where no actual token counts exist
buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope called twice on the same record -> returns identical recordDigest both times (deterministic); WHY: digest stability is required for future receipt binding

adversarial.desc: buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) where record has apiKey, secret, authorization, bearerToken, password, credentials, accessToken, refreshToken fields injected at multiple nesting depths (top-level, nested in provider, nested in usage.raw, nested in arrays) -> builder rejects ALL of them; deep scan of JSON.stringify(envelope) confirms zero matches against the full FORBIDDEN_FIELD_NAMES set; WHY: adversarial attacker tries to smuggle secrets through multiple nesting paths

buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) where field names use mixed case to evade denylist (ApiKey, API_KEY, rawPrompt, RawPrompt, PROMPT, AuthorizationHeader) -> builder still catches them (case-insensitive denylist match); WHY: case-variant evasion is the most common denylist bypass

buildUsageEvidenceEnvelope(record) where record contains field named content (in the denylist) at top level -> rejected/omitted even though content could be benign in other contexts; WHY: denylist is name-based not value-based, so even innocuous values under forbidden names are rejected by design

items.title: Receipt-reference fields on the authority block
items.context: Extend the record authority block (record.ts) to allow nullable receiptId plus receiptSubjectKind and receiptSubjectId (both nullable), while KEEPING the existing rule that local records have receiptVerified=false and receiptId=null by default. Update the validator so a local record still requires receiptVerified=false; receiptId/receiptSubjectKind/receiptSubjectId may be non-null only together (a referenced receipt) but that alone does NOT make it verified. Tested: a local record validates with the nullable fields; a record claiming receiptVerified=true without going through the gate is rejected or only allowed via the gate.

items.title: Verification gate (pluggable verifier; default keeps unverified)
items.context: Add verifyUsageReceipt(envelope, signedReceipt, verify) where verify is an INJECTED async/sync function (signedReceipt, envelope) -> { verified: boolean, subjectKind?, subjectId? }. Only when verify returns verified=true AND the subject binding matches the envelope does the gate return an authority block with receiptVerified=true + receiptId + receiptSubject*. Otherwise it returns receiptVerified=false. The usage-ledger module does NOT import the authority-signing module (verifier is injected) — preserves zero cross-module imports. Tested: injected verifier true+matching-subject -> verified; true+mismatched-subject -> NOT verified; false -> not verified.

items.title: Negative controls (cannot be tricked into verified)
items.context: Implement + test the spec's negative controls: transport accepted=true is NOT verification; a provider response with real token counts is NOT verification; a local JSONL hash chain is NOT verification; a copied receiptId without an injected verifier confirming signature+subject is NOT verification. In every case authority.receiptVerified stays false. Each negative control is a distinct smoke assertion.

items.title: Smoke/test suite wired + no regression
items.context: Add packages/main/src/tasks/usage-ledger-authority-smoke.ts (follow existing *-smoke.ts; ✓/✗, non-zero exit; temp dir, no pollution), wired as npm test:usage-ledger-authority. Cover the envelope (privacy-safe, has digest), the nullable receipt-ref fields validating, the verification gate (verified only via injected verifier + subject match), and all negative controls. Assert usage-ledger still imports ZERO other modules (no authority-signing import). Build green; full ledger suite (usage-ledger/-adapter/-estimate/-diagnostics/-dispatch/-budget) no regression; node bin/lattice.js validate.
